verified.what: T036 blocking defect FIXED (in-session CultureProvider.Switch had no effect in the real MAUI host)
verified.command: root-cause repro (dotnet console, ExecutionContext boundary model) + code fix + dotnet build + dotnet test full suite
verified.result: Root cause confirmed by a deterministic repro: CultureInfo.CurrentCulture/CurrentUICulture are AsyncLocal-backed; MauiProgram.RunStartupSequence pinned them on the startup thread, which shadows the DefaultThreadCurrent* globals on the Blazor renderer's execution context, so Switch updated the globals but every queued render kept reading the stale pinned value (only a process restart re-pinned). FIX: MauiProgram.RunStartupSequence and CultureProvider.Switch now set ONLY CultureInfo.DefaultThreadCurrentCulture / DefaultThreadCurrentUICulture (plain process-wide statics) - never the per-context CurrentCulture/CurrentUICulture. Repro proves that with no per-context override anywhere, a render on a separately-captured ExecutionContext reads the new culture. Build: 0 warnings / 0 errors. Full suite: 2068/2068 pass across all six projects (UI.Tests 635, +1 new regression guard CultureProviderTests.Switch_DoesNotPinAPerContextOverride_SoLaterGlobalChangesStillTakeEffect; Core 751, Reports 236, Localization 28, Data 158, Integration 260).
warnings: Live in-app re-verification of T036 (first-run /language-select -> /setup renders in the chosen language in the same session, both themes) and a re-confirm of T037 are still PENDING - bUnit renders synchronously so it cannot reproduce the ExecutionContext-boundary failure; the fix is proven at the mechanism level (repro) + unit/integration level (green suite), not yet re-watched in the real WebView2 host.

concerns.note: BLOCKING DEFECT found in T036 live verification: in-session language switching (CultureProvider.Switch, the central mechanism of spec 029) does not work in the real MAUI WebView2 host. Confirming a language on /language-select persists it and navigates on with no restart, but the destination renders in the OLD language - the new one only appears after a full app restart, i.e. the same user-visible symptom as issue #361. Startup resolution incl. the new no-DB preference tier is fine. Suspected root cause: CultureInfo.CurrentUICulture is AsyncLocal-backed; MauiProgram pins an explicit value on the root execution context at startup; Switch sets CurrentUICulture on the (unwinding) click-handler context and DefaultThreadCurrentUICulture process-wide, but the Blazor renderer keeps the startup-pinned CurrentUICulture, so IStringLocalizer never sees the change. bUnit tests (T007/T008/T024) and integration V22 pass because they render synchronously on the same context that calls Switch. Fix belongs in US1 T004/T016 + US2 T027 (a real switch mechanism that the renderer honours - e.g. re-resolve/reassign on the renderer dispatcher, or forceLoad navigation), plus a test that actually exercises a cross-context render. Out of scope for Phase 6 polish; needs its own debug+fix+test pass. T036 and T037 left unchecked.
concerns.resolution: FIXED 2026-09-02. The suspected root cause was correct. A deterministic ExecutionContext-boundary repro confirmed it, and the fix removes the per-context pin at BOTH sites: MauiProgram.RunStartupSequence and CultureProvider.Switch now assign ONLY CultureInfo.DefaultThreadCurrentCulture / DefaultThreadCurrentUICulture (plain process-wide statics), never CurrentCulture / CurrentUICulture. With no AsyncLocal override anywhere, every render reads CurrentUICulture straight through to the globals, so an in-session Switch is visible on the very next render regardless of which execution context runs it. New regression guard CultureProviderTests.Switch_DoesNotPinAPerContextOverride_SoLaterGlobalChangesStillTakeEffect. Docs updated (CLAUDE.md Localization, adding-a-language.md sec 9, contract, research.md Decision 2 correction, data-model.md). Build 0/0; full suite 2068/2068. Live in-app re-verification of T036/T037 in the real WebView2 host is still pending (bUnit cannot reproduce the EC-boundary failure).
